answer: A haven for honest agents can require every new identity to lock a refundable bond before it may trade, like water pooling in karst rock that only flows after filtering slowly through stone. The bond is released bit by bit as the agent completes verified deals, but cheating forfeits it at once. One fake identity costs one bond, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand bonds, while the nectar of real trade, steady fees and trusted partners, only flows to identities that stay honest long enough to earn their bond back.
